title: Beautiful Cookware That Requires Special Care to Keep Its Looks
text:
Beautiful Cookware That Requires Special Care to Keep Its Looks. This ALL-CLAD MC2 PROFESSIONAL MASTER CHEF 7-PIECE COOKWARE SET is drop-dead gorgeous. It is meticulously designed, machined, and hand-finished. However, it's a poor choice for me, because (1) my kitchen has a ceramic-top electric range, (2) it's heavier than my all-stainless-steel cookware, and (3) it requires hand-washing and a lot of extra care to keep it looking beautiful.

In general, aluminum cookware is the most energy-efficient, which is why "stainless steel" cookware usually has an aluminum core. Aluminum cookware is also lightweight. However, cookware made entirely from aluminum poses some toxic risk in regular use, because minute amounts of aluminum can leach into food during cooking (particularly into acidic foods like tomatoes).

This All-Clad cookware has a stainless steel interior that won't react with food. Thus it's completely safe for all cooking. It cooks efficiently, because it has an all-aluminum core plus an all-aluminum brushed exterior. However, it isn't particularly lightweight. The 9-inch All-Clad frying pan from this set weighs 1 lb. 9.9 oz., while my 9-inch Cuisinart stainless steel frying pan with aluminum-core bottom weighs 1 lb. 6.6 oz.

My ceramic-top electric range is not friendly to aluminum cookware, because aluminum has a fairly low melting point. The manual for the electric range suggests using extra caution when cooking with aluminum cookware, because aluminum can leave scuff marks on the cooktop, and because a pan allowed to boil dry can melt, fuse with the cooktop, and severely damage the cooktop. Of course it's fine to use this All-Clad cookware on a ceramic-top stove, but the cook needs to exercise particular care (1) to never turn the heat on under an empty pan, and (2) to follow the All-Clad recommendation and always use low or medium heat, except when boiling water. (The recommendation to use low or medium heat is NOT just for ceramic-top ranges, because high heat can warp any cookware.)

However, the main reason that I'm disappointed with this All-Clad cookware is that it requires so much extra care to maintain its stunning appearance. The All-Clad instructions include the following cautions: (1) to avoid the formation of white dots or pits in the cookware, bring water to a boil or wait for foods to begin cooking before adding salt; (2) to prevent water spotting, rinse in hot water and dry immediately; and (3) to prevent discoloration, avoid overheating (produces brown or blue spots), remove food films before reheating, and avoid high-iron-content water. In addition, for ordinary cleaning, the stainless steel interior should be cleaned with a paste of fine powder cleanser, washed in hot soapy water, and dried immediately. (You musn't use oven cleaners, oven cleansers, or chlorine bleach.) The aluminum MC2 exterior should be cleaned with commercial aluminum cleaner, and rinsed in lukewarm water.

In short, this cookware is "not recommended for dishwasher use". Because this All-Clad cookware is beautiful, but requires pampering to stay that way, I rate it at 3 stars ("It's okay" on the official Amazon scale).
